q: What is the appearance of chlorine at r.t.p.?
explain: Chlorine is a pale yellow-green gas at room temperature and pressure.

q: After sodium reacts completely with water, Universal Indicator is added to the solution. What colour does it turn?
explain: Sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali, so the indicator turns purple (high pH).

q: Lithium, sodium and potassium all react with water to form an alkaline solution. Which ion in the solution makes it alkaline?
explain: The metal hydroxide dissolves to release hydroxide ions, OH⁻, which make the solution alkaline.

q: Which statement about copper(II) and iron(II) compounds is correct?
options: Both can be coloured because they are compounds of transition elements.
Both are white because they contain metal ions.
Both are unreactive because the metals are unreactive.
explain: Compounds of transition elements are generally coloured, such as blue copper(II) and green iron(II) compounds.

q: Fluorine is at the top of Group VII. Which prediction is most likely to be correct?
options: It is a very reactive pale yellow gas.
It is an unreactive dark solid.
explain: Halogens are most reactive at the top of the group, and the elements get paler and less dense up the group.

q: Which change is the oxidation of an iron(II) ion?
explain: Oxidation is loss of electrons: Fe²⁺ loses one electron to form Fe³⁺.

q: In which part of the Periodic Table are the transition elements found?
options: on the far right, next to the noble gases
in the central block between Groups II and III
on the far left, in Group I
at the top of Group VII
explain: Transition elements form a block of metals between Group II and Group III.

q: Calcium is in Group II. What is the charge on a calcium ion?
explain: Group II atoms have two outer electrons, which they lose to form 2+ ions.

q: Which pair of solutions would react together?
options: aqueous iodine and aqueous potassium bromide
aqueous iodine and aqueous sodium chloride
aqueous bromine and aqueous sodium chloride
aqueous bromine and aqueous potassium iodide
explain: Only a more reactive halogen can displace a less reactive halide ion: Br₂ is more reactive than I₂.

q: Strontium, Sr, is in Group II. Which formula is most likely for strontium chloride?
explain: Group II elements form 2+ ions and chloride is Cl⁻, so two chloride ions balance one Sr²⁺ ion.

q: What is the electronic configuration of an argon atom?
explain: Argon has 18 electrons; its outer shell holds 8 electrons and is full.

q: Which description fits a transition element?
options: a non-metal with a low melting point and colourless compounds
a metal with a low melting point and white compounds
a metal with a high melting point and coloured compounds
explain: Transition elements are metals with high melting points and coloured compounds.

q: What is the name of the compound with the formula Fe₂(SO₄)₃?
explain: The two Fe ions balance three SO₄²⁻ ions (total 6−), so each Fe is 3+.

q: The compound FeCl₂ is named iron(II) chloride. What is the formula of iron(III) chloride?
explain: Iron(III) forms Fe³⁺, which needs three Cl⁻ ions to balance the charge.

q: Which statement about lithium, sodium and potassium is correct?
options: They are hard metals with very high melting points.
They are soft metals that can be cut with a knife.
They are dense metals that sink in oil.
explain: Group I metals are soft enough to cut, and they have low melting points and low densities.

q: What is the formula of rubidium chloride, given that rubidium is in Group I?
explain: Group I metals form 1+ ions, so Rb⁺ combines 1 : 1 with Cl⁻.

q: Which element in Period 3 is a non-metal?
explain: Sulfur is on the right-hand side of Period 3 and is a non-metal; the other three are metals.

q: An atom of an element in Group III has how many outer-shell electrons?
explain: The group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons for these groups, so Group III has 3.

q: Which statement correctly compares iron with sodium?
options: Iron has a higher melting point and a higher density.
Iron has a lower melting point and a higher density.
Iron has a higher melting point and a lower density.
Iron has a lower melting point and a lower density.
explain: Iron is a typical transition metal with a high melting point and high density; sodium is soft with a low melting point and a low density.

q: Why is chlorine more reactive than iodine?
options: A chlorine atom has more outer electrons than an iodine atom.
A chlorine atom has more electron shells than an iodine atom.
A chlorine atom attracts an extra electron more strongly than an iodine atom.
A chlorine atom loses electrons more easily than an iodine atom.
explain: Chlorine's outer shell is nearer the nucleus, so the incoming electron is attracted more strongly.

q: Which row correctly shows the oxidation numbers of iron in the two compounds?
explain: FeSO₄ contains Fe²⁺ with SO₄²⁻, and Fe₂(SO₄)₃ contains Fe³⁺ ions.

q: Which two elements are most likely to have similar chemical properties?
explain: Calcium and strontium are both in Group II, so their atoms have the same number of outer electrons.

q: Which row correctly describes the element sulfur?
explain: Sulfur has six outer electrons (Group VI) and gains two electrons to form S²⁻.

q: Which Group I metal is the most reactive?
explain: Reactivity increases down Group I, so of these three potassium is the most reactive.

q: Which statement is a property of transition elements and their compounds?
options: They have very low melting points.
explain: Transition element compounds are typically coloured, for example blue copper(II) sulfate.

q: Aluminium is in Group III and Period 3. What is the electronic configuration of an aluminium atom?
explain: Three shells are occupied (Period 3) and there are three outer electrons (Group III): 2,8,3.

q: Which explanation of the unreactivity of neon is correct?
options: Its outer shell has 7 electrons and needs one more.
Its outer shell is full, so it neither gains nor loses electrons nor shares them easily.
Its outer shell has 1 electron which is lost easily.
Its atoms are joined in pairs by covalent bonds.
explain: The configuration of 2,8 is stable, so neon does not form ions or covalent bonds.

q: Which formula represents a molecule of chlorine?
explain: Halogens are diatomic: two atoms are joined by a covalent bond in each molecule.

q: Why is potassium more reactive than lithium?
options: Its outer electron is closer to the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.
Its outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.
It has more outer electrons to lose than lithium.
Its atoms have fewer protons than lithium atoms.
explain: A potassium atom has more shells, so the single outer electron is held less strongly and is lost more readily.

q: Which mixture shows no reaction?
explain: A halogen only displaces a less reactive halogen; iodine is less reactive than chlorine, so it cannot displace it.
